items.quote: But for VKT, the sales -- definitely VKT buys APIs from SMS. So definitely, the sales of INR40 crores that you see are from that sales from SMS Pharma to VKT Pharma. And from Life Sciences, SMS buys some intermediates and raw materials.

items.statement: Operating cash flows increased sharply to 103.6 crore in FY26
items.quote: Operating cash flows increased sharply to 103.6 CR.

items.statement: Free cash flow generated in FY26 was around 42.28 crore
items.quote: So the free cash flows for generated in the previous year was around 42.28 crores.

items.statement: Working capital stressed in FY26 due to higher inventory and stretched receivable cycle, leading to higher borrowing and interest cost; expects significant improvement in FY27 as inventory and receivable cycles normalize.
items.quote: During the full year, working capital was stressed mainly because of the higher inventory, which we carried and the demand washout, which happened in the first quarter last year, and we carried the higher inventory through the Q4. items.quote: Working capital intensity is expected to improve significantly as inventory and the receivable cycles improves. We expect to improve operating and free cash flow generation in FY27.

items.quote: No, 7,800 tons, we require roughly INR35 crores.

items.statement: CMD says next year (FY28) capex for 2,400 tons LFC will be around INR60 to INR70 crores.
items.quote: next year when we go for a bigger project, that is for 2,400 tons, that time we are looking at investment of say around INR60 crores to INR70 crores.

items.quote: This year it will be by debt-only, and next year will be by debt and equity.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of INR334 crores achieved in FY26 due to improved working capital management
items.quote: We have delivered operating cash flow of INR334 crores during FY '26 on the back of improved asset utilization, operational efficiency and better working capital management.

items.statement: FY26 operating inflow reached INR1,049 crores, cash flow from operations INR271 crores, free cash flow before new project investment INR224 crores
items.quote: For FY '26, operating inflow reached to INR1,049 crores. Cash flow from operations stood at INR271 crores. Free cash flow before new project investment was INR224 crores.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance including investments stood at around Rs. 99 crores.
items.quote: Our cash and bank balance including investments stood at around Rs. 99 crores.

items.statement: Working capital increased due to higher revenue and inventory requirements; free cash flow was negative in Q4 FY26 as funds were absorbed by working capital.
items.quote: Regarding this increase in working capital: was it proportionate to the growth in sales, or were there other underlying changes, specifically, did the working capital cycle lengthen? For instance, did debtor days or inventory days increase? Could you please shed some light on this?

items.statement: Management expects working capital to turn positive within two quarters by shifting sales to organized corporate clients with reliable payment cycles.
items.quote: Within approximately two quarters, we will have converted a significant portion of our operations. Therefore, as we engage with corporates specifically with all the organized players in the sector if we transition our existing labor-based engagements with them to an outright contractual basis, our transformation from the unorganized to the organized sector will accelerate commensurately.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was negative in FY26 due to investment in receivables and inventory to fund 29% revenue growth with working capital at 65-68 days
items.quote: you can see the cash flows from operating activities , mainly because of the investments that are going into the receivables as well as inventory is negative in the current year.
